SEM-003.reopened_reason: SEM-003 was incorrectly reported as narrowly_verified. The card asks for Subject.Object.SemanticRole.Kind aliases, which implies four SEMANTIC dimensions drawn from a real taxonomy. The implementation instead derived all four segments from raw digest bytes, so every dimension was semantically empty. A dry run over eight operations produced eight distinct kind values when all eight are operations and must share one; eight distinct roles from a closed vocabulary that does not exist; and unrelated subjects for read_head and append_event even though both live in the same module. The tests verified collision-freedom, reserved-value safety and determinism, all of which pass while the thing carries no meaning. Mechanics were proven; intent was not.

evidence.claim: DEFECT: segments are digest bytes, not taxonomy. _candidate_stream seeds subject/object/semantic_role/kind from digest[0..3] modulo 254, so no segment has a system-wide stable meaning.

evidence.reference: dry run over eight operation entities
evidence.claim: distinct kind values [3, 25, 55, 56, 73, 114, 142, 224] for eight operations that must all share one kind value; distinct roles [24, 75, 134, 142, 149, 154, 216, 223] from a closed role vocabulary that does not exist.
The schema bounds segments to 1..254 but defines no vocabulary, so a conforming record can be produced that is semantically meaningless.

RETAINED as mechanics coverage only. These tests still prove zero collisions, 0/255 reserved enforcement and deterministic round trip, but they cannot prove semantic correctness and must not be read as if they do.
Locator record contract created at the card's declared candidate owner path; it is the only place a filesystem location appears in the semantic model.
Relation record contract created with a typed relation_kind enum, and target_entity_id nullable only where external_target is supplied.

ACCEPTANCE MET: a path edit changes the locator and never the entity identity. relocate replaces the locator, derives a distinct locator_id, keeps exactly one current locator per (entity, kind), and leaves identity_basis and entity_id untouched.

ACCEPTANCE MET: no dangling relation endpoints. Dangling and retired endpoints are refused at registration and re-checked on demand, so an endpoint retired after acceptance surfaces as a reported dangling relation rather than a silently broken edge.

Prior behavior is the defect being repaired: query_project_map_evidence builds locator as an inline path string with no entity binding, and stable_id folds in the project map revision so locator identity moves with the revision.
located_at edges are derived from current locators by bind_locators and never asserted independently, so a location edge cannot contradict the locator it reflects.
